title: Uber: Leading engineering through an agentic shift - The Pragmatic Summit
summary: Uber's developer platform leaders describe background agents, AI code review, test generation and migration tooling, plus adoption, measurement and rising cost problems.

assertions.quote: We saw about a maybe a 10 to 15% bump in overall dev velocity.

verdicts.note: The 55% figure comes from a 2022 controlled experiment on one small JavaScript task, not a survey; field studies find much smaller average gains (~10-25%).

assertions.quote: the accuracy of these tasks was much higher compared to the more ambiguous workloads.

verdicts.note: Background agents do produce usable PRs for well-scoped chores, but merge rates vary widely and many PRs need iteration; 'most of the time' is optimistic.

assertions.quote: They're spending more and more time in planning and code review because there's so much more code being generated

verdicts.note: Surveys and studies (e.g. Faros, Google) report increased PR volume and review load with AI adoption.

assertions.quote: Like these are all things that to have an effective agent have organizational memory it needs to start to get access to.

verdicts.note: Relevant org context plausibly cuts rework, but the cited 50% token / one-shot result is a single vendor test, not independent evidence.

assertions.quote: almost a 3x rate of quality versus something that would be generated from your typical generic agent.

verdicts.note: Filtered pipelines like Meta's TestGen-LLM show real gains, but the comparative evidence is mostly company-internal.

assertions.quote: we needed to run a big program to create a scalable version of how we handle large-scale change.

verdicts.note: Migration case studies (Google, Amazon Java upgrades, Airbnb) got their scale from pairing LLMs with deterministic tooling and validation rather than free-form generation.

assertions.quote: The more successful um technique that that we've applied is actually just sharing wins.

verdicts.note: Reports of token-maxing and resentment support it, but some mandated rollouts (e.g. Shopify, Coinbase) report adoption gains; evidence is anecdotal either way.

assertions.quote: these are activity metrics, right? These are not necessarily business outcomes.

verdicts.note: DORA 2024/25 and Faros 2025 found individual output up while organizational delivery metrics stayed flat or worsened; review and integration become the bottleneck.

assertions.quote: since 2024, our our costs have gone up at least 6x.

verdicts.note: Token-heavy agentic use has raised costs at many firms, but the figures are self-reported and vary widely by company.

assertions.quote: the right model to form the plan for the uh for the project. And then, lower cost but still pretty effective models

verdicts.note: Model strengths do differ by task in benchmarks and practice, but the specific pairing is personal preference and shifts each release.

assertions.quote: these decisions need to be revisited on a pretty regular basis.

verdicts.note: Tool-use and long-horizon capability jumps in 2025 changed effective workflows (chat-with-RAG to agentic loops); consistent with practitioner reports.
